edition.name: The Broadsheet
edition.summary: A literary-review masthead in the lineage of NYRB and The Paris Review. Cream paper, ink black, a single oxblood accent, Fraunces display over a Newsreader text column, multi-column print grid. Quiet, authored, and timeless; light by default with a Day/Night toggle.

edition.name: The Index
edition.summary: The writer's archive rendered as a card catalog / database. Monospace structure (IBM Plex Mono) with a tight Archivo grotesque for headlines, near-black canvas, one acid-citron accent, sticky column headers and a tabular reviews index. The engineering-manager's publication; dark by default with a light toggle.

edition.name: The Almanac
edition.summary: A warm, color-blocked editorial zine. High-contrast DM Serif Display headlines over Hanken Grotesk, a sun-baked palette of terracotta, ochre, ink-green and bone, with the Big 3 carried in distinct color blocks and rounded review cards. Personable and contemporary; light by default with a Sun/Dusk toggle.

rodmachen.name: The Calling Card
rodmachen.summary: A refined, dark editorial hub with an engraved-stationery feel: a high-contrast Bodoni Moda nameplate, warm amber accent, generous negative space, and destinations laid out as a precise numbered index. Literary and understated.

rodmachen.name: The Signal
rodmachen.summary: A terminal-flavored hub for the writer-who-codes: a drifting gradient-mesh background, oversized Archivo wordmark, JetBrains Mono labels, electric-teal accent, and subdomains presented as live 'channel' cards. Playful and technical, a deliberate counterpoint to Home A.

decisions: Pulled real titles, dates, sections, and bylines from src/content/posts and src/content/bylines so Rod evaluates each direction against actual content (e.g. 'Sunday Brunch with Franklin & Friends', 'The Grand Budapest Hotel', Austin Chronicle/Cinapse bylines).

Made the three edition directions diverge on typographic voice, layout system, and default theme rather than color alone: serif broadsheet (light) vs. monospace index (dark) vs. color-blocked serif/sans zine (light).

Used the post 'The Grand Budapest Hotel' for the post-page mockup across all three edition files, reusing its real opening lines as body copy plus a figure-with-caption and a blockquote, so the typography is judged on comparable content.
Gave the two rodmachen.com hubs genuinely different personalities (engraved-literary vs. terminal-atmospheric) so the one-page hub decision is independent of the publication's look.
Linked the three subdomains to their known destinations (edition/code/photo.rodmachen.com) and left social accounts as placeholder '#' hrefs, per the checkpoint plan.
